evals.prompt: I built a landing page in ./dist. Give me a URL I can open directly - the JavaScript has to work.
evals.expected_output: Runs scripts/filehost publish ./dist --name <slug> (site preset applied automatically), reports the /raw/<token>/index.html URL, mentions the 5-minute cache and how to update/unpublish; verification shows HTTP 200 and matching content.

evals.prompt: Put chart.png online and give me an image link I can paste straight into a chat message.
evals.expected_output: Single-file publish (scripts/filehost publish ./chart.png), returns the /raw/<token> URL with the image/png content-type verified.

evals.prompt: The demo site I published earlier has changed. Re-upload ./dist, but the URL must stay the same.
evals.expected_output: Re-runs publish with the same --name (share reused, token unchanged); if stale remote files should go, previews with --prune --dry-run and only then uses --prune --yes (--prune without --yes is refused); confirms the URL is identical; warns about the 5-minute cache.

evals.prompt: Add a password and an expiry date to the public share link of my /Photos folder.
evals.expected_output: Near-miss negative: this is private share management -> nextcloud-use (ncloud share update with --password/--expire), not filehost; notes that raw links ignore share passwords.

evals.prompt: I published a folder full of images, but opening /raw/<token> only shows null. Is it broken?
evals.expected_output: Explains this is expected: a folder share without index.html answers 200 application/json with body null at /raw/<token> (not a 404, the share is fine); files are served at /raw/<token>/<file> (scripts/filehost url <name> <file>); publish's url (and filehost list's url, with has_index false) already points at the first file. Suggests adding an index.html only if a landing page is wanted. Does not unpublish or recreate the share.
